r1-handoff.title: Handoff compliance
r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Handoff satisfied, independently reproduced (not merely trusted). force_reap: one-line library call spine_rail._binding_transaction(Path(project_dir), lambda reaped: reaped); zero edits to spine_rail.py (empty git diff --stat). Read spine_rail.py:397-436 directly: _binding_transaction loads raw, computes reaped=_reap_binding_entries(raw, now), calls mutate(reaped), persists only if new_map != raw -- confirming an identity mutate genuinely persists the load-time reap. TestForceReap::test_innocent_a_released_targets_entry_is_gone_immediately re-run in isolation (2 passed): asserts the fixture target reads status=='released' BEFORE force_reap runs (precondition sanity), then the binding entry is gone immediately after, read via spine_rail.load_binding (not a later transaction). Paired negative TestForceReap::test_violating_an_active_targets_entry_is_retained confirms an active target survives -- proving the reap is conditional, not a blanket wipe. _release_child_plans: read the full function body (scripts/spine_lifecycle.py, appended after _advance_and_release) -- all three safety properties present as shipped code: (1) LINEAGE -- declared_children built from task.child_checklist resolved relative to work_dir, both declaration-time and scan-time candidates realpath-resolved and is_relative_to-checked; an active JSON not in declared_children is left alone and appended to unclaimed_active (line ~412-415), never proximity alone. (2) HONEST NON-OWNER RELEASE -- caller_id is read exclusively from the PARENT spine's own engine_session.session_id (loaded from spine_path); the per-candidate scan loop only reads the child's engine_session.status, never its session_id; grep confirms no session.get('session_id') read anywhere in the function. Release goes through _engine_call(['--file',...,'release','--session-id',caller_id,'--force','--reason',reason]) -- the same choke point _advance_and_release uses; checklist_engine.main appears exactly once in the module (line 661, inside _engine_call; grep -n 'checklist_engine.main' shows 4 docstring-prose hits plus the one real call). (3) ESCAPE REFUSAL -- both the child_checklist declaration loop and the work_dir scan loop resolve candidates via Path.resolve() and refuse (continue) unless resolved.is_relative_to(resolved_work_dir); confirmed via the independently re-run symlink negative test. All 9 new tests (2 ForceReap + 7 ReleaseChildPlans) re-run individually and pass; full suite independently re-run: 104 passed (matches claimed 95->104, +9).

r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/g2-review/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/g2-review/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from g2-review alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

triage_candidates.statement: Non-blocking: scripts/spine_lifecycle.py's module docstring (top of file) narrates the pure/impure split through _advance_and_release but was not extended to describe force_reap/_release_child_plans. Deferred deliberately -- g3 adds a third closeout primitive (finish_work) to the same section, so a single docstring update after g3 lands avoids two touches. Flag for g3/its reviewer so it is not missed.

Non-blocking variant of property 3 not covered by a named test: _release_child_plans walks work_dir with Path.rglob('*.json'), which can traverse a symlinked DIRECTORY (not just a symlinked file) during recursion. Verified this is not a live safety gap -- every discovered candidate is still realpath-resolved and is_relative_to-checked before any release, so a file reached via a symlinked directory that escapes work_dir is still refused by the same guard. The gap, if any, is only in whether such an escaped file gets reported at all (it would currently surface, correctly refused, same as a symlinked file). Low priority; the handoff's close criteria and required evidence name only the file-symlink case.

Non-blocking cleanup candidate: _release_child_plans repeats the same realpath-resolve-then-containment-check block in its declaration loop and its scan loop. A small helper (e.g. _resolve_within(path, boundary) -> Path | None) would give property 3 one implementation instead of two kept in sync by hand. Could be combined with g1-review's tc1 (the analogous _advance_and_release duplication) into one later cleanup pass. Low priority; does not affect correctness or either safety property this gate exists to verify.
